natural_body: 40% SMB discount: +31% signups, +18% rev, -12% ret; judge at renewal

first.rationale:
The two measured declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the highest-leverage single slot is the one that attacks the actual regression rather than the competitor's price move. Promotional pricing is the emotionally tempting response to the competitor launch, but memory_73 is the one inherited record that carries its own unresolved caveat: +31% signups and +18% revenue against -12% retention, explicitly tagged 'judge at renewal'. That verdict has not been rendered, so treating it as a win would convert an open question into a settled fact and would trade sustainable qualified revenue for a signup spike in exactly the price-sensitive segment that churns. I am not spending verification budget there because the caveat is already legible in the memory itself.

I am spending both pulls on memory_31 and memory_86 because they are my primary evidence and they may not be independent. Both describe onboarding/signup simplification lifting activation, consolidated 40 days apart with sources archived; memory_86 reads like it could be a re-consolidation of the same underlying experiment as memory_31 rather than a second confirmation. If the archive shows one original record behind both, my evidence base is a single study, not a replicated finding, and I should drop to a small guarded test. If they are genuinely distinct experiments, the standard experiment scale is warranted.

Downstream value risk flagged on two counts. First, memory_31's mechanism is 'cutting required fields at signup' — fields removed at signup are often qualification and routing data, so an activation lift can mask a decline in lead quality and in the enterprise demo-request path that memory_44 says produces the better pipeline. Activation is a proxy; qualified revenue is the objective, and this intervention can move the proxy while degrading the objective. Second, both source memories predate the competitor launch, so the population they were measured on may no longer be the population I am acting on. Instrumentation therefore must include a holdout and downstream renewal/qualified-pipeline tracking, not just first-week activation, and I will not read a completion-rate lift alone as success.

Activation_messaging (memory_91) is the fallback if verification collapses the onboarding evidence, since it targets the same decline without touching qualification fields. Referral_incentive (memory_57) is sound but addresses established customers, not the segment that is regressing.
